name: SuperCDMS
notes: Two INSPIRE experiment records exist for this programme: SuperCDMS-Soudan (recid 1298909, FNAL-E-0891) and SuperCDMS-SNOLAB (recid 1357671, FNAL-E-0947). Both phases are represented here as one experiment:supercdms record with dated intervals and two facility_roles/detector placements, per the wave-3 brief's guidance to record the Soudan phase as an interval rather than a separate experiment id. external.inspire_experiment cites the current (SNOLAB) recid. The Soudan-phase interval is deliberately kept non-terminal (status `active`, not `completed`) because A3 forbids a non-terminal interval after a terminal one on the same entity; the fact that Soudan operations ended in 2015 is recorded in that interval's note and end date instead.

No source fetched this session explicitly states a predecessor relationship between experiment:cdms-ii and experiment:supercdms in citable text; lineage is left empty rather than asserted from memory (A17). Known gap worth revisiting once an official SuperCDMS history page is found.
DOE Critical Decision milestones between the 2014 INSPIRE approval and the 2018 construction start (if any) are not recorded: no source fetched this session gives them.

physics_goals.quote: The collaboration is searching for dark matter particles with masses smaller than ten times the mass of the proton.
value: Detect dark matter particles with masses smaller than about ten times the mass of the proton via nuclear recoils in cryogenic silicon and germanium crystals

summary.plain: SuperCDMS looks for dark matter using silicon and germanium crystals cooled almost to absolute zero. It first ran at the Soudan mine in Minnesota until 2015, and its bigger successor is now starting up nearly a mile underground at SNOLAB in Canada, aiming at very light dark matter particles.
summary.technical: Cryogenic Ge/Si ionization-and-phonon dark matter search; SuperCDMS Soudan (Soudan Underground Laboratory, ~2009-2015) was succeeded by SuperCDMS SNOLAB, now under commissioning/early science with 24 detector crystals cooled to 15-30 mK, targeting sub-10-proton-mass WIMPs; full-sensitivity science operations are planned for 2027.

unique_capabilities.quote: For SuperCDMS, that temperature is just tens of millikelvins, or thousandths of a degree above absolute zero.
value: Phonon- and ionization-sensing cryogenic crystal detectors optimized for very low-mass WIMP nuclear recoils, operated near 15-30 mK
